messages.subject: I get tons of errors during compilation, and I do not know what is wrong...
parts:
Hi all,

Thanks for STAN and for the amazing support!! I just have one (big) problem. I am trying to run a model, but I keep getting a fatal error when I source it. I have checked the stan model hundreds of times and I do not find the error. I attach here the model, and also a text file with all the errors that I get...Can anyone help me, please? I have been able to run other more complicated models without problems, but I do not know what is going on here.

Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: I get tons of errors during compilation, and I do not know what is wrong...
parts:
On Sunday, March 3, 2013 6:59:48 PM UTC-5, Carlos wrote:
Thanks for STAN and for the amazing support!! I just have one (big) problem. I am trying to run a model, but I keep getting a fatal error when I source it. I have checked the stan model hundreds of times and I do not find the error. I attach here the model, and also a text file with all the errors that I get...Can anyone help me, please? I have been able to run other more complicated models without problems, but I do not know what is going on here.

The primary problem is this line:

PRED[n] <- A*Y1[n] + dot_product(MUS,X[n]) + dot_product(B[n+1].*Q, Z[n]);

B is a (N+1)xK matrix and Q is 1xK. But B[n+1] is the n+1th element of B. Perhaps you meant row(B, n+1) ?

Similar, Z[n] is the nth element of Z rather than the nth row. Perhaps you meant transpose(row(Z,n)) ?

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: I get tons of errors during compilation, and I do not know what is wrong...
parts:
On 3/4/13 4:27 PM, Carlos wrote:
> Thanks! Definitely, that was one of the issues. The other issue was in the line where I had
>
> |
> F <- 2*phi - 1;
> |
>
> since phi is a vector. I think I will never be able to set properly matrices and vectors in STAN :D I need to get rid of
> my MATLAB-way-of-thinking...

What doesn't work like in MATLAB? Is it just that a variable
gets a single type that's declared? Otherwise, our matrix
syntax is very MATLAB-like, or at least that was the intention.

If F is a vector and phi is a vector, then your expression
should work, and set F so that:

F[n] = 2 * phi[n] - 1

It won't work if F is a row vector and phi
is a vector or vice-versa. It will work if they're both
matrices of the same dimension.

- Bob
